newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Parliament discusses lower fuel consumption tax.
newsitem.headline: Greek Parliament discusses lower fuel consumption tax.

text.p: A parliamentary finance committee discussed on Wednesday an amendment to a draft bill extending a reduced special consumption tax (EFK) on heating fuel that was submitted by Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

The amendment which lowers the special consumption tax on diesel by 8,500 drachmas per 1000 litres during October 21 to December 31 1996 will cost state coffers about 12.6 billion drachmas in foregone revenues, the General Accounting Office said.
The reduction brings it down to 33,500 drachmas per 1000 litres.
The reduction aims to protect the incomes of consumers of this fuel who invariably happen to be low and middle income classes.
It will cushion price hikes resulting from firm oil prices, said a report signed by Papandoniou, explaining the rationale for the tax cut.

But PASOK's parliamentary representative and former deputy finance minister Dimitris Georgakopoulos disagreed with the move saying the tax reduction would increase the budget deficit by 32 billion drachmas.
He said the four drachma drop in the price of fuel would benefit the petroleum companies, parliament sources told Reuters.
